h1:
5 Most Popular Hotels
Chiang Mai
That We've Reviewed
heroSub: Five of Chiang Mai's most popular hotels that we've reviewed in depth — a luxury boutique next to Wat Chedi Luang in the heart of the old town, a riverside all-suite with an infinity pool, a flower-garden resort out in Hang Dong, a riverside boutique with a Sky Bar, and a Lanna boutique under a 200-year-old tamarind tree. Prices start at roughly ฿2,400–4,200/night.
introH2: 🏙️ What kinds of popular hotels does Chiang Mai have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Chiang Mai is a fun city to choose a place to stay, because every neighborhood gives a completely different experience — some people want to walk out the hotel door and run straight into Wat Chedi Luang and the walking street, some want to wake up, open the curtains, and watch the Ping River drift past the balcony, some want to escape the city and sleep in a quiet flower garden, and some want to soak up real Lanna charm under a big shade tree in the middle of the old town. · A lot of people book popular hotels on reputation alone, without checking whether the location and style actually fit their trip — and only realize once they arrive that it isn't the right match. · This article gathers five of Chiang Mai's most popular hotels that we've reviewed in depth, covering the old town, the Ping riverside, and Hang Dong outside the city — each one drawn from reading real guest reviews, telling you the upsides and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites, and giving you the direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Chiang Mai has no metro, but the city is compact — calling a Grab or hopping in a red truck (songthaew) is easy and cheap. · From Chiang Mai airport into town takes about 10–15 min. · The stay areas in this article: The old town (inside the moat) — walk to the temples and the walking street, get around with barely any need to call a ride. · The Ping riverside, Wat Ket area — quiet and waterside, a 3–10 min walk to Warorot Market and the Night Bazaar. · Hang Dong, toward Samoeng — a garden resort outside the city, the quietest option, needing about a 30 min drive into town.

entries.type: Boutique Luxury 5-Star · Heart of the Old Town
entries.name: Chala Number 6
entries.badge: 🏆 Highest score · Next to Wat Chedi Luang
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old town · under a 3 min walk to Wat Chedi Luang
entries.addr: 6/6 Prapokklao Road, Phra Sing, Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: If there's one hotel that nails the idea of "stay in the heart of the old town without trading away the peace and quiet," people who go to Chiang Mai often tend to name Chala Number 6 first — and it's the highest-scoring hotel in this article at 9.3 from over 710 reviews on Trip.com. · The hotel sits on Prapokklao Road in the Phra Sing–Si Phum area, in the middle of the moat zone, and it's under a three-minute walk to Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phan Tao, with the Sunday walking street running right through the neighborhood. · The thing every review agrees on is that the moment you walk back inside the hotel's walls, the traffic and tourist noise vanish in a surprisingly complete way — there's a garden, an outdoor pool that many people say looks beautiful at sunset, a whirlpool corner to soak in, and a wooden rice barn that serves free afternoon tea with snacks, and at certain times a short sample massage to try. · The rooms are another point that sets it apart from a typical boutique, because an entry-level room like the Junior Suite is already roughly 55 sqm and up, decorated in bright contemporary Thai tones, with many rooms opening straight out to the garden. · The hotel opened in 2017 and went through a major renovation in 2023, so the rooms still look fresh. · What gets the most consistent praise is the service — staff are warm and attentive to small details, to the point that many people feel like an important guest. · Honest caveats from the reviews: soundproofing between rooms still isn't good enough, so you may hear the next room or the hallway at times; rooms without a balcony have a small window and little light; the breakfast room is fairly small; and the lane in front of the hotel is narrow, so if you drive yourself you should ask about parking in advance even though free parking is available. · Bottom line: it's best for couples and anyone who wants a 5-star feeling on an attainable budget, right in the heart of the old town, where you can step out the door and start exploring immediately.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room that opens onto the garden — it gets better light and is quieter than a room next to the hallway. · And don't forget to ask the afternoon tea times at check-in so you don't miss it.
pros: Score of 9.3, the highest in this article, from over 710 reviews on Trip.com
Heart-of-the-old-town location, under a 3 min walk to Wat Chedi Luang and the walking street
Entry rooms 55 sqm, larger than average · garden pool that's lovely in the evening
Free afternoon tea and service that many reviews say is better than the price suggests
cons: Soundproofing between rooms still isn't good enough — you may hear the next room
Rooms without a balcony have a small window and little natural light (from reviews)
Small breakfast room, may mean waiting for a table when busy · narrow lane in front

entries.name: Cross Chiang Mai Riverside
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ping riverside · Wat Ket · 5–10 min walk to Night Bazaar
entries.addr: 369/1 Charoenrajd Road, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Cross Chiang Mai Riverside is a luxury 5-star hotel on the Ping River in the Wat Ket area that many people still remember by its former name, X2 Chiang Mai Riverside — it opened in 2017 before rebranding to Cross under the Cross Hotels & Resorts group, and had a major renovation in 2022. · What sets it apart from the usual riverside stays is its all-suite concept: the whole hotel has just 29 rooms, and every one is a suite starting from 51 sqm and up — noticeably larger than the standard rooms of most 5-star hotels in Chiang Mai — and every room has a private balcony. · The highlight people talk about most is the rooftop infinity pool, whose edge looks like it meets the horizon, with a wide view out over a bend in the Ping River and the city; many reviews rank it among the best-view pools in the area, especially in the early morning when the pool is still quiet and at sunset. · Up top there's also a poolside bar and a gym with a river view, while the X2 Spa has treatment rooms including a couples' room. · Breakfast at the Oxygen restaurant gets frequent praise for being varied and freshly made, good quality for a small hotel. · It's a MICHELIN Guide member, with a score of 9.2 from 233 reviews on Trip.com and as high as around 9.4 on some platforms. · The location works well too, because it's about a 5–10 min walk across the bridge to the Night Bazaar — you get both riverside quiet and convenience. · Honest caveats: the building has been open since 2017, so some spots are starting to show their age; some reviews fault the layout or the cleanliness of certain rooms as not quite fully 5-star; in-house dining options are limited; and river-view rooms fill up fast in high season. · It's best for couples and anyone who wants a luxury riverside hotel with large, well-designed rooms at a more attainable price than the other luxury heritage names in the same area.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If the view matters to you, specifically request a River View or Grand Suite river-view room when you book, because Garden View looks onto the garden or the building instead. · And heading up to the rooftop pool at sunset is when the view is at its best.
pros: All-suite, 29 rooms, spacious from 51 sqm, every room with a balcony
Rooftop infinity pool with a Ping River view, one of the best-view pools in the area
MICHELIN Guide member, score of 9.2 · breakfast frequently praised
Riverside location, a 5–10 min walk across to the Night Bazaar
cons: Building open since 2017, some spots starting to show their age (from reviews)
Some reviews fault the layout/cleanliness of certain rooms · limited dining options
Only 29 rooms, so river-view rooms fill up fast in high season

entries.type: Garden Resort 5-Star · Outside the City, Hang Dong
entries.name: Flora Creek Chiang Mai
entries.badge: 🌸 Resort in a 15-rai garden · Pool villas
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Hang Dong · toward Samoeng · about 30 min into town
entries.addr: 90 Moo 4, Ban Pong, Hang Dong, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: If the top two hotels sell a heart-of-the-city and a riverside location, Flora Creek Chiang Mai chooses to sell the opposite — actually "getting out of the city." · It's a 5-star resort built on over 15 rai of flowers and plants in the Hang Dong area, toward Samoeng, a zone full of fields-edge cafes and mountain views. · It opened in 2016, renovated in 2019, has 70 rooms, scores 8.8 on Agoda from 349 reviews, and around 4.5/5 on TripAdvisor. · From the real reviews, the people who come away happy tend to be three groups: couples who want a quiet, romantic stay, families who don't want to get up early to fight for parking in town, and people on a workation for a long change of scenery. · Rooms range from a Superior Garden View at around 33 sqm up to a 140 sqm Pool Villa with a private pool, which many people happily pay extra for so they can soak in the pool watching the mountains in the evening. · The heart of the resort is the outdoor pool, positioned to face the line of mountains — the spot photographed for social media the most, because morning and evening light is lovely and the mountain shadows reflect on the water. · There's a spa set in the garden, a free gym, and green space to stroll all day. · The service also gets praise for friendly staff who help arrange the shuttle and recommend places to go. · Honest caveats from the reviews: distance is the thing to weigh most — the resort is about 25–30 min from the old town and Nimman, and there's a shuttle into town on a schedule, but the runs are limited, so if you don't rent a car you'll have to rely on rides the whole time; in-resort dining isn't as varied as a hotel in the city; and ground-floor rooms next to the garden may get some damp or insects, as is natural for a stay in the middle of a garden. · It's best for people who want "Chiang Mai, the relaxing version" more than "Chiang Mai, the city-sightseeing version," and who plan a longer, unhurried 2–3 night stay.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Check the shuttle schedule into town before you arrive and plan your trip around the runs, or rent a car — it changes the trip entirely, because the Hang Dong–Samoeng area has plenty of cafes and flower gardens. · Pool villas are few and very popular, so book ahead.
pros: Resort in a 15-rai flower garden, quiet, with mountain views, genuinely good for relaxing
Spacious rooms all with a private balcony/terrace · pool villas have a private pool
Mountain-view pool and a nice-atmosphere spa · helpful staff (from reviews)
Good value compared with 5-star resorts in the city at a similar price
cons: Far from the city, about 25–30 min from the old town/Nimman, always reliant on a ride
Limited shuttle runs into town · in-resort dining isn't very varied
Ground-floor rooms next to the garden may get some ants or insects, naturally (from reviews)

entries.name: Sala Lanna Chiang Mai
entries.badge: 🌆 Ping-riverside Sky Bar · Most accessible price
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ping riverside · Wat Ket · 3 min walk to Warorot Market
tags: 🌆 Rooftop Sky Bar with river view
entries.addr: 49 Charoenrat Road, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Sala Lanna Chiang Mai is a small 4-star design boutique with just 16 rooms, set on the Ping River on the Wat Ket side, and it's the place with the most accessible starting price in this article at around ฿2,400/night. · The hotel is a clean white building, contemporary in design, blending in just-enough woodwork details and the warm Lanna tones. · Its clearest selling point is the rooftop Sky Bar overlooking both the Ping River and the Doi Suthep mountain range, which nearly every review mentions positively — many say the cool, late-afternoon light is the best time of day here, and a spot like this is hard to find at this price. · It's also listed in the Michelin Guide under accommodation, scoring 8.8 from 62 reviews on Trip.com and 4.4/5 on TripAdvisor. · Most rooms look onto the Ping River and many have a private balcony to sit and sip coffee in the morning, listening to the water. · The location is a strong point too, because it's about a 3 min walk to Warorot Market (Kad Luang), and crossing the Nawarat Bridge or the Iron Bridge gets you to the city side, with the Night Bazaar about a 5–7 min walk. · The riverside Wun Lamun restaurant serves khao soi that reviews praise as rich, and the warm, close service of a small hotel is a strength reviews mention often. · Honest caveats from the reviews: some rooms are starting to show their age and some decor looks worn; the ground-level pool isn't large, and the rooftop pool had a closure for repairs after the 2025 earthquake, so check the latest status before booking; and drinks at the Sky Bar are fairly pricey, with some cocktails not as strong as expected. · It's best for couples and travelers who want the Ping-riverside atmosphere and a river-view rooftop on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room with a direct Ping River view (Deluxe River View and up), because the view is the main selling point. · Go up to the Sky Bar mainly for the view, order drinks in moderation, then go for a real meal at Warorot Market or a spot in the Wat Ket area nearby, which is better value.
pros: The most accessible starting price in this article, around ฿2,400/night
Rooftop Sky Bar with a Ping River and mountain view, a sunset spot reviews praise
Ping riverside in the Wat Ket area, a 3 min walk to Warorot Market, easy crossing into the city
Listed in the Michelin Guide · khao soi at Wun Lamun and warm service
cons: Some rooms are starting to show their age, some decor looks worn (from reviews)
Rooftop pool had a closure for repairs after the 2025 earthquake · ground-level pool isn't large
Drinks at the Sky Bar are pricey, cocktails not as strong as expected

entries.type: Boutique 4-Star · Contemporary Lanna, Heart of the Old Town
entries.name: Tamarind Village
entries.badge: 🌳 Most reviews · Under a 200-year-old tamarind tree
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old town · Rajdamnoen Road · right on the Sunday walking street
entries.addr: 50/1 Rajdamnoen Road, Sri Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Tamarind Village is a boutique hotel that's long been talked about as an "oasis in the heart of the old town," and it's the place with the most reviews in this article — over 2,100 on TripAdvisor with a 4.6/5 score, ranked around 38th out of more than 540 hotels in Chiang Mai, with a Travelers' Choice award and a score of 8.6 on Trip.com. · What sets it apart from a typical hotel is the story of the place itself: the whole hotel was designed around a tamarind tree over 200 years old that still stands and spreads its shade in the middle of the courtyard to this day, and it's the source of the name "Tamarind." · The design is the work of Ong-ard Satrabhandhu, a Thai architect who reinterpreted Lanna techniques and materials, and it once received a UNESCO Asia-Pacific award for cultural heritage conservation. · Many reviews describe walking through the bamboo tunnel into the inner courtyard as like stepping into another, peaceful world, even though just outside is the busy Rajdamnoen Road. · The location is what nearly every review ranks as its number-one strength, because the hotel sits right on the Sunday walking street, about a 5 min walk to Tha Phae Gate, with Wat Phra Singh and Wat Chedi Luang about 7–8 min away, so many people say they barely needed to call a ride the whole trip. · There's an outdoor pool ringed by Lanna-style buildings and a garden, a spa using Lanna-style treatments, and the Ruen Tamarind restaurant where you can dine under the tamarind tree in a nice setting — many reviews say the food is genuinely good. · Honest caveats from the reviews: the price is fairly high relative to the rooms, which aren't very large (standard rooms around 25 sqm); the building has been open since 2002, so it leans on heritage charm rather than newness; some rooms are fairly dark and the air-con in some rooms isn't strong enough on very hot days; and on Sunday nights the walking street opening in front of the hotel gets lively and noisy. · It's best for people who value design, genuine Lanna character, and peace and quiet in the heart of the old town, and who are willing to pay extra for the atmosphere and service.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're sensitive to noise, especially on Sunday nights, ask for a room facing the courtyard or garden. · If light and space matter to you, choose Lanna Deluxe and up, which are larger and usually have a balcony. · And try the old-town walking tour the hotel arranges, which reviews praise often.
pros: The most reviews in this article, over 2,100 · TripAdvisor 4.6/5 Travelers' Choice
Designed around a 200-year-old tamarind tree by Ong-ard Satrabhandhu (UNESCO award)
Right on the Sunday walking street, walk to Tha Phae Gate and the temples, all of it
Garden pool, a Lanna spa, and the Ruen Tamarind restaurant that reviews praise as tasty
cons: Price is fairly high relative to room size (standard rooms around 25 sqm)
Building open since 2002, some rooms fairly dark, air-con in some rooms not strong (from reviews)
On Sunday nights there's noise from the walking street in front of the hotel

advice.bodyHtml: → Chala Number 6 ฿3,500, next to Wat Chedi Luang, under a 3 min walk, garden pool, free afternoon tea, score of 9.3, the highest in this article

advice.bodyHtml: → Flora Creek Chiang Mai ฿2,500, a resort in a 15-rai flower garden in Hang Dong, mountain-view pool, pool villas with a private pool, shuttle available

advice.head: Want a riverside atmosphere on a budget
advice.bodyHtml: → Sala Lanna Chiang Mai ฿2,400, a Ping-riverside boutique, rooftop Sky Bar with a river view, Michelin Guide, a 3 min walk to Warorot Market, the most accessible price

advice.bodyHtml: → Tamarind Village ฿4,200, a Lanna boutique under a 200-year-old tamarind tree, right on the Sunday walking street, the most reviews at over 2,100

advice.head: On a tight budget but want a good score at a light price
advice.bodyHtml: → Sala Lanna ฿2,400 or Flora Creek ฿2,500 — both start under three thousand baht but deliver atmosphere and a score of 8.8 from real reviews

advice.bodyHtml: → Cross Chiang Mai Riverside ฿4,200, all-suite with an infinity pool · or Sala Lanna ฿2,400, a boutique with a Sky Bar — both on the Ping River on the Wat Ket side, with an easy walk into the city

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting prices from the standard-room price range and may change by date and season; we recommend checking the real price and comparing 3 sites before every booking. · The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms — we did not stay ourselves. · Cross Chiang Mai Riverside was formerly named X2 Chiang Mai Riverside — it's the same place. · Sala Lanna had a period of rooftop-pool repairs after the 2025 earthquake; check the latest status before booking. · During festivals (Yi Peng/Loy Krathong in Nov, Songkran 13–15 Apr, New Year) prices rise and rooms sell out fast, so book 1–2 months ahead. · Chiang Mai has no metro; a Grab or a red truck is convenient, and the airport into town is about 10–15 min. · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travelers often ask about popular Chiang Mai hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which popular Chiang Mai hotel is the best?
faq.a: It depends on your travel style. · If you go by score, Chala Number 6 at 9.3 is the highest in this article, a luxury boutique next to Wat Chedi Luang in the heart of the old town. · If you want luxury riverside with large rooms, Cross Chiang Mai Riverside is all-suite with an infinity pool. · If you want to escape the city and relax, Flora Creek is a garden resort. · If you want riverside on a light budget, Sala Lanna has a Sky Bar. · And if you want to experience real Lanna, Tamarind Village has the most reviews at over 2,100.

faq.q: ❓ How much do popular Chiang Mai hotels cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at roughly ฿2,400–4,200 per night for a standard room. · The most accessible are Sala Lanna from ฿2,400 and Flora Creek from ฿2,500. · Mid-range is Chala Number 6 from ฿3,500. · And the top end is Cross Chiang Mai Riverside and Tamarind Village from ฿4,200 (suites and pool villas are much higher than this). · Festival-period prices may be above normal.

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in for a first trip to Chiang Mai?
faq.a: The old town (inside the moat) suits a first-time visitor — walk to the temples and the walking street, get around with barely any need to call a ride (Chala Number 6, Tamarind Village). · The Ping riverside, Wat Ket area suits people who want riverside quiet but still within walking distance of Warorot Market and the Night Bazaar (Cross Chiang Mai Riverside, Sala Lanna). · Hang Dong, outside the city suits people set on relaxing at a quiet resort but needing a ride into town (Flora Creek).

faq.q: ❓ Are Cross Chiang Mai Riverside and X2 Chiang Mai Riverside the same place?
faq.a: Yes, they're the same place. · The hotel opened in 2017 as X2 Chiang Mai Riverside before becoming Cross Chiang Mai Riverside with the rebranding of the Cross Hotels & Resorts group, and it was renovated in 2022. · Some platforms still show the old X2 name — same building, same location, a 5-star MICHELIN Guide member.

faq.q: ❓ Which popular Chiang Mai hotel is good for couples and honeymoons?
faq.a: Every place in this article leans toward a couple-friendly atmosphere. · The ones reviews mention most for riverside romance are Cross Chiang Mai Riverside, all-suite with large rooms and an infinity pool, and Sala Lanna, with a Sky Bar overlooking the river. · If you want quiet in a garden, Flora Creek has pool villas with a private pool. · If you want a Lanna atmosphere in the heart of the old town, Chala Number 6 and Tamarind Village suit couples who like walking the temples together.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a Chiang Mai hotel?
faq.a: Many hotels in this article are small properties (16–82 rooms, some just 29 rooms), so they fill up fast. · During high season (November–February) and the Yi Peng/Loy Krathong festivals, book 1–2 months ahead or more. · Other times, 2–4 weeks is enough. · Every platform has Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in a price like that first if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
